blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Persistent Records**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Long-Term Memory, § Persistent Records
blocks.md: When a multi-session repair agent stores repository source files, test execution logs, and its own progress notes in a single undifferentiated memory pool, a later session can easily treat an unverified hypothesis or an old `r17` test log as current ground truth about the code. Those artifacts play different roles in the repair. The repository source defines what the code looks like at a given commit. An execution log records how a test behaved under specific runtime parameters against that commit.

questions.q: The section **Persistent Records** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: Neighborhoods grow geometrically with traversal depth, so multi-hop retrieval bounds edge types, direction, depth, and visited nodes before ranking.

Every read is a bounded request answered by an envelope that reports scope, snapshot, completeness status, and per-item provenance, and an empty result proves nonexistence only for a complete search of the declared scope.

Persistent records are roles in an evidence chain (source of record, observation log, agent-written memory, retrieval index), not storage tiers, and any claim is validated against its source of record.

Repeated retrieval or re-summarization adds no independent evidence, so preventing a withdrawn or unverified claim from persisting needs a provenance graph over derived records whose invalidation cascades.

points: **Persistent memory record**: A stored cross-session record has an explicit role and provenance; retrieval does not turn stored text into an authoritative instruction.
